questions.q: Does the paper's exact cut placement (Fig. 5) match a canonical minimum-cut algorithm on the VD circuit graph, or is it hand-selected?
questions.basis: Section III-B describes cutting between 'diagonalizing gate fragments and original-circuit fragments' but does not specify whether this is optimal in the CutQC / KaHyPar sense or a heuristic.
questions.next_steps: Extract the paper's Fig. 5 cut and compare against qiskit-addon-cutting's automatic cut finder on the same RealAmplitudes(4q, reps=2) + Z_0Z_1 + Z_1Z_2 + Z_2Z_3 + Z_0Z_3 MaxCut Hamiltonian; check whether the reported CNOT counts (11,14,17,17) match the automatic partitioner.

questions.q: Is the FakeHanoi noise-model version dependence controlled? Different Qiskit-Aer versions produce different NoiseModel.from_backend outputs.
questions.basis: The paper does not report Qiskit / Aer version numbers. Post-Qiskit-1.0, FakeHanoi was reworked into qiskit-ibm-runtime.fake_provider, changing default T1/T2 defaults and gate-error tables.
questions.next_steps: Author correspondence to obtain (a) qiskit version, (b) qiskit-aer version, (c) FakeHanoi commit hash / calibration date used. Or re-run on the current FakeHanoi and report the version-conditional numbers.

questions.q: How sensitive is the VD+CC error (0.058) to the RZZ(-pi/3.5) crosstalk angle?
questions.basis: The paper picks -pi/3.5 to model 'gate crosstalk' between same-layer adjacent CNOTs, but does not justify the specific angle or provide a sweep. Under basic+GCT, VD alone jumps from 0.180 to 0.276 (54% worse), while VD+CC stays at 0.058 — a stark difference that hinges on the crosstalk model.
questions.next_steps: Sweep the RZZ angle in {-pi/2, -pi/3, -pi/3.5, -pi/4, -pi/6, 0} and re-generate Table I column 'basic+GCT'; check whether VD+CC's error stays flat or the flatness is an artifact of the chosen angle.

questions.q: Does the reconstruction overhead (4^K for K wire cuts) actually manifest in shot budget for the 4-fragment scheme, or do they use asymptotic sampling?
questions.basis: The paper reports 4 fragments with CNOT counts 11,14,17,17 (Table I footnote 7) but does not report shot counts per fragment. QPD reconstruction with K cuts requires ~4^K shots to achieve the same statistical precision.
questions.next_steps: Author correspondence for shot counts per fragment; independently estimate whether their reported 0.058 error is dominated by shot noise or by (residual) coherent noise. A back-of-envelope: for K=3 cuts (4 fragments = 3 cuts), overhead ~64x. If they ran 8192 shots/fragment monolithic equivalent, actual shot budget was ~5e5 fragment-shots — feasible.

questions.q: Does the method still work when the noise-free classical simulator is replaced by a second noisy quantum device (as the abstract hints)?
questions.basis: The abstract says 'while the remaining fragments are efficiently simulated on a noiseless classical simulator' — but for larger problems the classical part will not be efficient. The paper does not evaluate a two-device split.
questions.next_steps: Extend to a Qiskit-Aer noise model on ALL fragments (not just the noisy state-prep fragment) and re-measure Table I. If VD+CC error degrades to near baseline, the paper's benefit is limited to problems where the diagonalizing subcircuit fits inside classical statevector reach (< 30 qubits total).
